title: Float values in refinement list don't sort properly.
body:
**Describe the bug 🐛**
Float values in refinement list don't sort properly.

**To Reproduce 🔍**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Pick a test index
2. Add `size` attribute and put values like 9, 9.5, 10, 10.5, 11…
3. Add `size` as a facet filter
4. Add refinement list to your page:

```
search.addWidget(
  instantsearch.widgets.refinementList({
    container: '#brand-list',
    attributeName: 'size',
    sortBy: ['size:asc'],
  })
);
```

https://codesandbox.io/s/420yp9lyn0

**Expected behavior 💭**
Should be sorted 9, 9.5, 10. It's 9, 10, 9.5 instead.

**Screenshots 🖥**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1834312/45288514-26702c80-b4eb-11e8-8440-6c2f15d6a318.png)

**Environment:**
 - OS: Mac
 - Browser: Chrome
 - Version 68.0.3440.106

**Additional context**
Please ping me back when it's solved so I can contact the customer who reported it.

comments.body: @bobylito I think this issue should be addressed in the [JavaScript helper](https://github.com/algolia/algoliasearch-helper-js) since we leverage the `getFacetValues()` method in `connectRefinementList` ([see corresponding line →](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/694c82b9a2230b160f6f5a47bb7da355066cdf85/src/connectors/refinement-list/connectRefinementList.js#L336)).

> @bobylito I think this issue should be addressed in the JavaScript helper since we leverage the getFacetValues() method in connectRefinementList (see corresponding line →).

Yes that seems to be the place to fix 👍

Let's keep this issue for keeping track of the implementation at the IS.js level.
Thanks for the effort in handling this folks! I understand, super clear answers 🙌.

This can be solved by using sortBy with a parseFloat (otherwise it sorts alphabetically). As using numerical values for facets is not the main use case (because it usually will explode quickly in number of values, making a range more interesting), I'll close this issue for now.
